meta.basis: The priest 'cubitis super Altare positis, stans capite inclinato, distincte, reverenter et secreto profert verba consecrationis' over the Host, which he holds 'pollicibus et indicibus' (Ritus servandus VIII.5); 'he now bows over the altar, leaning the forearms on it' (Fortescue, l. 4871–4874). The chalice is still covered. The server lifts the chasuble and rings only at the elevations (VIII.6; Fortescue, l. 6384–6390, 6403), the thurifer incenses only then (VIII.8), and the torches are held from the Sanctus (Fortescue, l. 9613–9617).
